title: Capability contracts
description: The capability registry vocabulary, exact capability versions and the capability lock (05 §3, §6, §11; 09 §21). The registry itself is protocol/capability_registry.json.

CapabilityKey.description: A capability key (05 §6), lowercase snake_case, at most 64 characters. A capability contract is key@version.

CapabilityVersion.description: A capability contract version (05 §6): a positive integer. key@version is immutable in meaning once published; a breaking change takes a new version (05 §6, 'Capability version immutability').

CapabilityVersions.description: Exact capability pins, capability key to version (05 §3 requires.capabilities; 05 §6). A map, so one version per key: the canonical decoder rejects a repeated key, and canonical encoding sorts keys.

CapabilityLock.description: The exact capability lock of a compiled cartridge or deployment (05 §3 'Compatibility versions', §6, §11): every capability version it executes. capability_lock_hash (09 §21) is hash(lock) under loka-numeric-v1; format is the hash domain tag, and any change to this format takes a new tag. Resolving a manifest's requirements and registry dependencies into a lock is the compiler's job (R4).

CapabilitySpec.description: One registry entry (05 §6): a capability version, its portability, and its semantic residency from the residency matrix (05 §6 'Capability semantic residency matrix'). Portability limits residency (this table is the PM's adopted reading of 05 §6, not spec text): a portable capability is a portable semantic foundation or portable capability implementation, server_only is a Realm-only semantic capability, client_presentation_only is client presentation; authority-host coordination and authoring/certification are never capabilities (05 §6). A null residency is not yet classified. An Effect names the capabilities that may emit it (allowed_origins in protocol/effect_registry.json). A capability lists the commands, events and policy ops it owns (05 §6: a capability owns the commands, events and policies it introduces); each registered one has exactly one owning capability key, checked in test/loka/core/registries_test.exs. Only the portable branch has these fields for now; a server_only capability gains them with the first command, event or op it owns.

oneOf.description: Runs on every host, Story and Realm (05 §6).

host_adapters.description: The kernels that implement this capability; absent means none bound yet. An elixir entry on a portable_capability needs a differential (ADR-074 trigger, checked by bin/contracts.exs).

differential.description: The cross-kernel differential test for this capability (ADR-074).

commands.description: The Command types this capability owns, by name (CommandPayload type, command.schema.json); absent means none.

events.description: The DomainEvent types this capability owns, by name (EventPayload type, event.schema.json); absent means none.

policies.description: The policy operators this capability owns, by name (Policy op, policy.schema.json); absent means none.

oneOf.description: Realm-only; an offline_private cartridge cannot depend on it for gameplay (05 §6).
Presentation only, never gameplay legality or authoritative mutation (05 §6).

ResidencyClass.description: The six responsibility classes of the 05 §6 residency view ('Capability semantic residency matrix'). A capability's residency is one of the other four (CapabilitySpec); authority-host coordination and authoring/certification are never capabilities and appear only as Responsibility rows.

Responsibility.description: A row of the 05 §6 residency view that is not a registered capability (protocol/residency.json): a portable semantic foundation contract that both kernels must implement with golden cross-host parity, or a host or authoring responsibility named in 05 §6's 'Owns' column. fixtures lists the conformance files both kernels are tested against; an empty list means none is bound yet, never that none is needed. Host services are not made into gameplay capabilities by appearing here (05 §6).
